questions.stem: Choose the correct article: I waited for ____ hour at the station.
questions.explanation: Article choice between a/an depends on SOUND, not spelling. 'Hour' begins with a silent h and starts with a vowel sound /aʊə/ → 'an'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: My brother is ____ MBA from Delhi University.
questions.explanation: MBA begins with the sound /em/ — a vowel sound, so 'an'. Same logic for 'an MLA', 'an SMS', 'an X-ray'. Test SOUND, not letter.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: He is ____ one-eyed beggar.
questions.explanation: 'One-eyed' starts with the consonant sound /w/ → 'a'. Same with 'a university', 'a European', 'a useful thing' — all begin with /j/ or /w/ despite starting with a vowel letter.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: ____ Ganges is considered sacred in Hinduism.
questions.explanation: Rivers, oceans, seas, mountain ranges, gulfs, deserts — always 'the': the Ganges, the Pacific, the Himalayas, the Sahara. Single mountains and single lakes are exceptions (Mount Everest, Lake Victoria — no article).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: ____ honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take NO article. 'Honesty', 'love', 'patience', 'truth' in general contexts → no article. We WOULD use 'the' if the reference is specific: 'the honesty of this man is rare'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: Mount Everest is ____ highest peak in the world.
questions.explanation: Superlatives ('highest', 'best', 'tallest', 'largest') and ordinals ('first', 'second') always take 'the'. Also ranks that are unique: 'the president', 'the Supreme Court'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: She plays ____ piano beautifully.
questions.explanation: Musical instruments take 'the' when referring to playing them: 'play the piano', 'play the guitar', 'play the violin'. Sports, however, take NO article: 'play cricket', 'play football'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: ____ Netherlands is a small country in Europe.
questions.explanation: Most country names take no article ('India', 'Japan', 'Brazil'). Exceptions — countries that are PLURAL or have 'Kingdom/States/Republic' in the name take 'the': the Netherlands, the Philippines, the USA, the UK, the UAE.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: ____ poor need our help.
questions.explanation: Adjective used as a plural noun to refer to a whole class takes 'the': the poor, the rich, the elderly, the unemployed, the blind, the educated. Grammar label: adjective-as-collective-noun.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: He goes to ____ school every morning.
questions.explanation: When the institution is used for its PRIMARY PURPOSE, no article: 'go to school' (to study), 'go to church' (to pray), 'go to hospital' (as a patient — British usage), 'go to bed' (to sleep). 'Go to THE school' implies visiting the building for some other reason.
questions.subject: English
